sections.title: About FoldBridge
sections.body: FoldBridge connects residue-level RNA chemical-probing profiles from RMDB and RASP to experimentally resolved PDB chains. Each Entry keeps the source signal, sequence mapping, structure state, and confidence evidence together so you can move from an observed probing signal to the structure it maps onto.

sections.title: Data collection and alignment
sections.body: FoldBridge combines per-residue chemical-probing data from RMDB / RASP with experimentally resolved PDB chains. Each probing sequence is aligned to its corresponding chain, and only residues with resolved structural coordinates enter confidence scoring. Records without a usable mapping or signal are flagged or excluded rather than force-scored.

items.body: Parsed from the chain's dot-bracket secondary-structure annotation and aligned to PDB coordinates.
Computed per residue on the mmCIF structure with the Shrake-Rupley algorithm; author and label residue numbering are reconciled before joining.
Determined from inter-residue atom distances and used as ground truth for contact-based methods.

sections.title: Confidence labels
sections.body: A confidence label combines a measurement family with a calibrated recall tier. The family names the physical quantity measured; it is not a quality grade. The tier states how reliably the evidence recovers the deposited structure after quality gates and a permutation test.

items.body: Reagents that hit the Watson-Crick face of specific bases (DMS, CMCT, Keth-seq). Statistic auc_unpaired_vs_paired, positive class = unpaired: high signal means that base is unpaired.
SHAPE reagents that report 2′-OH flexibility on any of the four bases. Same statistic as A (auc_unpaired_vs_paired), positive class = unpaired: high signal means a flexible, likely unpaired residue.
Nucleases such as PARS / PARTE cleave paired stems, so the logic is reversed. Statistic auc_paired_vs_unpaired (= 1 − AUC), positive class = paired: high signal means paired.

Hydroxyl-radical and related probes (RL-Seq, HRF, Lead-seq, icLASER) report how exposed the backbone is. Statistic Spearman(reactivity, SASA): more signal should track more exposed surface. When SASA is missing it falls back to an AUC proxy (flagged PAIRING_PROXY_FALLBACK, and a hard cap keeps it out of STRONG).
Methods (MCA / MOHCA) that report which residue pairs sit close together in 3D. Statistic contact_pair_auc: near equals a hit.
Mutate-and-map approaches that infer an entire set of base pairs, scored against the reference pair set. Statistic pair-set F1 (precision / recall / F1).

sections.title: LSS confidence calculation
sections.body: LSS (Local Structure-Signal Support) is calculated for each (profile, PDB entry, chain) segment. It asks whether probing values agree with the paired/unpaired or geometric state in the deposited structure. A segment needs at least 15 evaluable residues, including 5 paired and 5 unpaired; otherwise it is UNDERPOWERED.

sections.title: Tier calibration
sections.body: Every valid segment is compared with shuffled structure labels to estimate an empirical p-value. STRONG requires p ≤ 0.05, AUC ≥ 0.70, at least 20 evaluable residues, self-containment ≥ 0.70 and conflict ≤ 0.25. MODERATE uses relaxed gates; evidence that does not beat chance is NOT_SUPPORTED.

items.body: Permutation-calibrated and satisfying every STRONG gate (p ≤ 0.05, AUC ≥ 0.70, n ≥ 20, self-containment ≥ 0.70, low conflict). The evidence strongly supports the structure.
Satisfies the relaxed gates (p ≤ 0.10, AUC ≥ 0.65, self-containment ≥ 0.50). The evidence supports the structure reasonably well. When uncalibrated it appears as MODERATE_CANDIDATE.
AUC clears the bar but the secondary gates (self-containment / conflict / sample size) do not; flagged auc_supported_but_not_self_contained.
The directional metric falls into the conflict band, or the conflict fraction is too high — the probing signal disagrees in direction with the structural truth and needs review.
Fails the evaluability gates (n_eval < 15, or fewer than 5 paired or unpaired). Too little data to draw a conclusion.
Not significant under the permutation test (p > 0.10): even a high-looking AUC is no better than chance once the labels are shuffled.

sections.title: Thresholds
sections.body: Most A/B/C cut-points (0.70 / 0.65 / 0.55) are operating values, not published thresholds. Only the RL-Seq Spearman cut-points (0.50 / 0.40 / 0.30) are literature-set. The registry labels each technology's threshold basis so values still awaiting calibration remain explicit.

sections.title: How to make a feedback
sections.body: We welcome your feedback, ideas, and suggestions. They help us keep FoldBridge useful, functional, and user-friendly. When possible, include the relevant page URL, PDB ID, chain, profile, or a screenshot so we can reproduce the issue.
